title: Error result
description: What any tool returns when it fails. Over MCP it is the result's text with isError set; on the CLI it is the single line on stderr. A rejected apply changes nothing and lists every failing op, not just the first. Every error says how to fix it.

reason.description: One stable code for the whole failure. For a single error it equals errors[0].code; a batch with several failing ops uses batch_rejected.

applied.description: apply, exec and recipe only: always 0. Nothing in a rejected batch was applied.

next.description: Calls or commands that would move forward, such as "read(space: 'auth-plan', ids: ['n-gateway'])" or "reflex agents approve".

code.description: Stable error codes. New codes are added in minor versions; a code never changes meaning.

count.description: A non-negative integer in the shared safe range.

op.description: apply only: the index of the failing op in ops.

field.description: The field at fault, as a JSON Pointer into the op or the input, such as '/from'.

msg.description: What went wrong, in one sentence, naming the closest valid value when there is one.

fix.description: What to change, in one sentence.

schema.description: invalid_props only: an excerpt of the extension type's schema.

example.description: invalid_props only: one valid example of the type's props.

pending_sends.description: How many Sends wait in this Agent's Inbox. Every tool result carries it. Drain them with wait_for_user(timeout_s: 0).
